newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

A ministerial team visited Langadu in Rangamati distict of Chittagong Hill Tracts where tribal Shahti Bahini rebels have killed up to 30 Bengali settlers and told residents the government is determined to restore peace in the region through political dialogue.

Colonel (retd) Farook Rahman was produced before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court and was placed on a seven-day police remand for interrogation about the November 3, 1975 killing of four top Awami League leaders in jail. The deaths followed kiling of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in a military coup on August 15, 1975.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said her government was determined to establish friendly relations with all neighbouring countries including China, where she is now on a five-day official visit.

Chief Minister of India's Assam state Prafulla Kumar Mahanta appreciated initiatives by Bangladeshi business leaders to open up economic relations between the northeastern states of India and Bangladesh

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has condemned the massacre of 30 Bengali settlers in Chittagong Hill Tracts by tribal rebels, saying it is a conspiracy to disturb the peace process her government has initiated. Opposition leader and former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia said she is shocked by the killings.
At least 50 people were killed and six vehicles damaged in clashes between students and villagers that forced the Shahjalal University in northeastern Sylhet district to be closed down.

The IMF has been pondering measures to help reduce debt burden of the heavily indebted low income countries, IMF resident representative in Dhaka Jan Bove said. He however said Bangladesh was not included in 41 heavily indebted countries on the IMF list.
The government has decided to constitute a 13-member legal aid committee to help the poor and downtrodden in the society who are deprived of proper justice.
